title: Repeated Games I: Perfect Monitoring
claims: Repeated interaction can create future incentives for cooperation.
The familiar discounted prisoner's-dilemma incentive condition applies only with specified payoffs, monitoring, strategies, and horizon.
uncertainties: Author notes are an authoritative introduction, not an empirical FW study.
No discount factor or equilibrium result is estimated for the proposed game.

title: Repeated Games III: Imperfect Private Monitoring
claims: Private observations complicate coordinated punishment and cooperation.
Specific examples show why conclusions from perfect public observation cannot simply be imported.
uncertainties: The course surveys results known in 2006; it is not a current exhaustive survey.
Proposed evidence-based trust updates are design choices, not a theorem from these notes.

title: Are people conditionally cooperative? Evidence from a public goods experiment
publisher: Urs Fischbacher, Simon Gächter, Ernst Fehr / Economics Letters; author-university copy
claims: The public-goods experiment identifies heterogeneous contribution patterns, including conditional cooperators and free riders.
uncertainties: Study proportions are not population estimates for EVE players or either militia.
Search-indexed original abstract and author publication listing were inspected; direct PDF open timed out.
Non-EVE laboratory setting limits external validity.

title: Transcript from an interview with Elinor Ostrom and Oliver E. Williamson
publisher: Nobel Prize / interview with original researchers
claims: Ostrom explains that her institutional principles describe regularities among durable systems rather than one universal prescription.
She discusses polycentric arrangements with multiple decision centers.
uncertainties: Precise publication day was not established.
Indexed transcript passages were inspected; subsequent direct open returned 403.
Applying these institutional insights to militia coalitions is an analogy, not an EVE finding.

title: Pay for Performance and Beyond
claims: Multitasking changes incentive design because agents allocate effort across interdependent activities.
Easy-to-measure and hard-to-measure tasks can compete for attention.
uncertainties: Search-indexed section IV of the original lecture was inspected; direct PDF open returned 403.
The proposed project-reward system is an application, not an optimal-contract solution.

title: Strategic Information Transmission
publisher: Vincent P. Crawford and Joel Sobel / Econometrica; Haverford-hosted original-paper copy
claims: A sender-receiver model with partly divergent interests permits partially informative communication.
Greater preference alignment can improve informativeness under the paper's assumptions.
uncertainties: The model's scalar information and equilibrium assumptions do not directly describe the full EVE war.
No literal human deception rates or real named-player traits are inferred.

title: The Motivational Pull of Video Games: A Self-Determination Theory Approach
publisher: Richard M. Ryan, C. Scott Rigby, Andrew Przybylski / Motivation and Emotion
claims: Four studies relate perceived autonomy, competence, and relatedness to enjoyment and future game play.
The results motivate distinguishing several dimensions of engagement.
uncertainties: This is not an EVE-specific burnout model.
No numeric fatigue or attendance coefficient in the proposed simulation is taken from this paper.
Relationships with fictional NPCs should not be equated with the paper's multiplayer social context.

title: Deterministic Network Interdiction
publisher: R. Kevin Wood / Mathematical and Computer Modelling; Naval Postgraduate School archive
claims: The interdiction model allocates limited resources to reduce an adversary's maximum feasible network flow.
The general problem is computationally difficult even under restricted resource assumptions.
uncertainties: Indexed original abstract and introduction inspected; direct archive open returned 403.
Game cargo-flow constraints are proposals; stargates do not inherit the paper's hypothetical edge capacities.
Full EVE transport includes routes absent from an internal FW graph.

title: Targeting, Deployment, and Loss-Tolerance in Lanchester Engagements
publisher: Michael P. Atkinson, Moshe Kress, Niall J. MacKay / Operations Research
claims: The paper extends Lanchester analysis with targeting, deployment constraints, and loss tolerance.
Elementary square-law reasoning assumes targeting, simultaneous deployment, and fighting conditions that are not universal.
uncertainties: Online-first publication is 2020-12-09; journal issue is January-February 2021.
This is not an empirically fitted EVE combat model.
Numerical military-force thresholds from the paper are not imported as game balance rules.

title: Monte-Carlo Planning in Large POMDPs
publisher: David Silver and Joel Veness / Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 23
claims: POMCP combines sampled beliefs and Monte Carlo planning using a generative simulator.
The paper reports results on particular large POMDP benchmarks.
uncertainties: No browser runtime or FW campaign performance is established by this paper.
A multi-actor adaptive strategic game is not automatically a stationary single-agent POMDP.

title: Loyalty Points
claims: LP are earned through eligible activities and spent in issuing-corporation stores.
uncertainties: Date is the displayed update date, not necessarily initial publication.
Store offers and conversion economics require dated game data.

Corporation LP-store purchases can spend corporation LP and ISK.
uncertainties: Launch rules do not establish all current tax rates or donation permissions.
The initial shared tax-rate description was superseded by independent LP tax capability.
The consulted locale URL contains English note text.

The update also exposes corporation palette information and renames the enlistment faction field.
uncertainties: API field names and response shapes must match the chosen compatibility version.
A public tax rate does not reveal a corporation's wallet, actual attendance, or internal agreements.

Announcement describes intended November 2023 features; later detailed implementations should be checked.

title: Manufacturing
claims: Manufacturing converts input items using blueprints at appropriate facilities.

There is no universal finite facility job-slot pool.
uncertainties: Date is the displayed update date.

A single strategic production queue is a UI abstraction.

uncertainties: No raw report series were independently analyzed for this section.
Regional and global aggregates do not identify militia wallets, industrial output, or motivation.
Nominal destruction values and price-index changes are not direct measures of military effectiveness.

Campaigns can have lasting game-world outcomes.
uncertainties: Date is the displayed update date.
Specific campaign objectives and outcomes are era-dependent; do not substitute a generic production contribution for official mechanics.
